problems.name: Climbing Stairs
problems.question: Given n stairs, you can climb either 1 or 2 steps at a time. Return the number of distinct ways to reach the top.

examples.explanation: Only one single-step climb is possible.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(1). Iterative DP keeps only the previous two counts.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(n). Memoized recursion computes each step count once.

problems.name: Min Cost Climbing Stairs
problems.question: Given cost[i] for stepping on stair i, return the minimum cost to reach the top when you may climb 1 or 2 steps each move.

examples.explanation: Start at index 1 and move directly to the top.
The optimal path uses the cheap stairs.
Start at either stair and reach the top for free.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(1). Iterative DP keeps the best cost for the previous two positions.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(n). Memoized recursion solves each position once.

problems.name: House Robber
problems.question: Given money in houses along a street, return the maximum amount you can rob without robbing adjacent houses.
problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(1). Iterative DP keeps take/skip best values.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(n). Memoized recursion computes each starting index once.

problems.name: House Robber II
problems.question: Given money in houses arranged in a circle, return the maximum amount you can rob without robbing adjacent houses.

examples.explanation: Rob houses with values 1 and 3 without touching both ends.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(1). Run linear robber twice over two ranges.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(n). Memoized recursion solves each range once.

problems.name: Decode Ways
problems.question: Given a digit string where A-Z maps to 1-26, return the number of valid decodings.
problems.constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 100; s contains only digits and may contain leading zero.

examples.explanation: It can be BZ, VF, or BBF.
A code cannot start with zero.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(1). Iterative DP keeps ways for the next one and next two positions.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(n). Memoized recursion computes each index once.

problems.name: Coin Change
problems.question: Given coin denominations and an amount, return the fewest number of coins needed to make that amount, or -1 if impossible.

examples.explanation: No coins are needed for amount zero.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(amount * coins.length); Space O(amount). Bottom-up DP computes minimum coins for every amount.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(amount * coins.length); Space O(amount). Memoized recursion solves each remaining amount once.

problems.name: Coin Change II
problems.question: Given coin denominations and an amount, return the number of combinations that make up the amount. Each coin may be used unlimited times.
problems.constraints: 1 <= coins.length <= 300; 0 <= amount <= 5000; answer fits in signed 32-bit integer.

examples.explanation: The combinations are 5, 2+2+1, 2+1+1+1, and five ones.
The empty combination makes amount zero.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(amount * coins.length); Space O(amount). 1D DP counts combinations by coin order.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(amount * coins.length); Space O(amount * coins.length). Memoized recursion uses coin index and remaining amount.

problems.name: Combination Sum IV
problems.question: Given distinct positive nums and target, return the number of ordered combinations that sum to target.
problems.constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 200; 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000; 1 <= target <= 1000; answer fits in 32-bit integer.
problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(target * nums.length); Space O(target). Bottom-up DP counts ordered totals.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(target * nums.length); Space O(target). Memoized recursion solves each remaining target once.

problems.name: Longest Increasing Subsequence
problems.question: Given an integer array, return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.

examples.explanation: Strict increase does not allow equal values.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n log n); Space O(n). Patience sorting tails use binary search.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n^2); Space O(n^2). Memoized recursion tracks index and previous index.

problems.name: Longest Arithmetic Subsequence
problems.question: Given an array, return the length of the longest arithmetic subsequence.
problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n^2); Space O(n^2). Hash maps store best length by difference for each ending index.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n^2 * D) after memoized pair states; Space O(n^2). Recursion extends a chosen difference.

problems.name: Partition Equal Subset Sum
problems.question: Given an integer array, return true if it can be partitioned into two subsets with equal sum.

examples.explanation: No subset sums to half the total.
Total is 12, but no subset makes 6.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n * target); Space O(target). 1D boolean DP tracks reachable sums.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n * target); Space O(n * target). Memoized recursion stores index and remaining target.

problems.name: Word Break
problems.question: Given a string and a dictionary, return true if the string can be segmented into a sequence of one or more dictionary words.
problems.constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 300; 1 <= wordDict.length <= 1000; words contain lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: No split covers the entire string.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n^3) with substring creation; Space O(n + dictionary). Bottom-up DP checks all cuts.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n^3); Space O(n + dictionary). Memoized recursion stores failed start positions.

problems.name: Perfect Squares
problems.question: Given n, return the minimum number of perfect square numbers whose sum is n.
problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n * sqrt(n)); Space O(n). Bottom-up DP computes best square count for each total.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n * sqrt(n)); Space O(n). Memoized recursion solves each remainder once.

problems.name: Integer Break
problems.question: Given integer n, break it into at least two positive integers and maximize the product of those integers.
problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n^2); Space O(n). Bottom-up DP tests all first split positions.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n^2); Space O(n). Memoized recursion solves each integer size once.

problems.name: Maximum Product Subarray
problems.question: Given an integer array, return the maximum product of a non-empty contiguous subarray.
problems.constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 20000; -10 <= nums[i] <= 10; product fits in 32-bit integer.

examples.explanation: The zero is larger than negative products.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(1). Maintain max and min product ending at the current index.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(n). Recursive scan carries max/min ending states through the array.

problems.name: Maximum Subarray
problems.question: Given an integer array, return the largest sum of any non-empty contiguous subarray.

examples.explanation: The only subarray is the array itself.
The full array has maximum sum.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(1). Kadane keeps the best ending sum and global best.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(n). Recursive scan carries current and best sums.

problems.name: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
problems.question: Given prices where prices[i] is the stock price on day i, return the maximum profit from one buy followed by one sell.
problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(1). Track minimum price and best profit.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(n). Recursive scan carries minimum price and best profit.

source.label: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock - LeetCode 121

problems.name: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock with Cooldown
problems.question: Given daily stock prices, return the maximum profit with unlimited transactions and a one-day cooldown after selling.

examples.explanation: Buy day 0, sell day 1, cooldown, buy day 3, sell day 4.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(1). Three state variables hold, sold, and rest are enough.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(n). Memoized recursion stores day and holding/cooldown state.

problems.name: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock with Transaction Fee
problems.question: Given daily stock prices and a transaction fee, return maximum profit with unlimited transactions where each sale pays the fee.

examples.explanation: One optimal sequence gains 6 after fees.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(1). Two state variables cash and hold are enough.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(n). Memoized recursion stores day and holding state.

problems.name: Delete and Earn
problems.question: Given nums, you may take a value x to earn x points per occurrence, but then all x - 1 and x + 1 values are deleted. Return maximum points.

examples.explanation: Only one number can be taken.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n + U); Space O(U), where U is max value. House Robber DP runs over value buckets.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n + U); Space O(U). Memoized recursion solves each value once.
